headline: High-risk default interaction: ChatGPT Desktop can feed sensitive content into Kestra workflows, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads files and clipboard, while Kestra can ingest files, messages, and workflow inputs. A shared workspace or copy-paste bridge lets attacker-controlled content from one side influence the other, but no direct automatic channel is documented. The pathway is plausible for both agents, not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF the operator copies Kestra-generated text into ChatGPT Desktop or saves it in a shared file
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads a file that Kestra later treats as workflow input
mitigations: Use separate folders for ChatGPT Desktop inputs and Kestra workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted workflow text into ChatGPT Desktop
Add a manual review step before Kestra consumes any AI-generated file
Label AI-generated artifacts as untrusted in filenames
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and Kestra can write logs, artifacts, notifications, and cloud data. If ChatGPT content is routed into Kestra outputs or logs, sensitive material can leak beyond the original context. The pair’s default surfaces make this a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop processes uploaded files or screenshots containing secrets
IF Kestra logs, stores, or notifies on those AI-derived inputs
mitigations: Redact secrets before sending content to ChatGPT Desktop
Restrict Kestra logging for AI-derived workflow steps
Store AI outputs in a separate, access-controlled bucket
Review notifications for sensitive payloads before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read access to files and clipboard, while Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and broad network egress. Both can touch shared files and mutable workflow artifacts, so concurrent edits or overwrites are plausible and can corrupt state or trigger unintended actions. The overlap is stronger than a read-only conflict.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or artifact path
IF Kestra writes files that ChatGPT Desktop is simultaneously reading or summarizing
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause Kestra writes while ChatGPT Desktop is inspecting files
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Keep Git or workflow state outside ChatGPT Desktop-visible paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can summarize or transform inputs, and Kestra can execute workflows, send email, Slack, PagerDuty, or cloud actions. If Kestra treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated summary can cascade into real operational actions. The downstream blast radius is large and defaults are not safe.
conditions: IF Kestra uses ChatGPT Desktop output as a workflow parameter or decision input
IF that workflow can send notifications or trigger cloud/SSH/Docker actions
mitigations: Require human approval before Kestra executes AI-derived steps
Add schema validation to ChatGPT outputs before ingestion
Limit AI output to advisory-only fields
Log the original source alongside the derived instruction
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in Kestra

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Kestra handles logs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications. If regulated data enters ChatGPT and then persists in Kestra logs or artifacts, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by ChatGPT Desktop and then stored in Kestra artifacts or logs
IF retention settings differ between the two systems for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to ChatGPT Desktop
Set short retention on Kestra logs and artifacts
Purge sensitive workflow outputs after use
Document which data classes may cross the boundary
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
